question: How does Django's authentication system work and how do you implement JWT authentication?
title: Django Authentication and JWT
direct_answer: Django's built-in auth: User model, session-based authentication. request.user is set by AuthenticationMiddleware from the session cookie. For APIs, session auth is impractical — use djangorestframework-simplejwt: users get an access token (short-lived) and refresh token (long-lived) by posting credentials. The access token is included in Authorization: Bearer headers. Simplejwt validates the token and sets request.user on each request without a database lookup.
interviewer_intent: Tests authentication pattern knowledge — session vs token, and the practical simplejwt setup that's standard in DRF projects.

sections.title: Django auth: session vs JWT
sections.content:
Django's built-in auth is session-based: user logs in, Django creates a session record in the database, sets a session cookie. Each request, the session middleware reads the cookie, looks up the session, sets request.user. Works great for server-rendered apps. For APIs consumed by SPAs or mobile apps, cookies are awkward — you want stateless token-based auth.

JWT (JSON Web Token): encodes user identity in a signed token. The server signs it with a secret key; anyone with the public key can verify it without a database lookup. Access tokens are short-lived (15min–1hr) to limit damage from theft. Refresh tokens are long-lived and stored securely — used to get new access tokens.

djangorestframework-simplejwt: the standard JWT package for DRF. POST to /api/token/ with credentials returns {access, refresh}. Include access token as Authorization: Bearer <token>. When it expires, POST to /api/token/refresh/ with the refresh token.

Custom user model: always define AUTH_USER_MODEL = 'myapp.User' before the first migration. After migrations, it's very hard to change. Add fields like phone, profile_image to the custom model, not a separate Profile model.

sections.title: JWT auth setup with simplejwt
sections.content:
# requirements: djangorestframework-simplejwt

# settings.py
INSTALLED_APPS = [
    'rest_framework',
    'rest_framework_simplejwt',
    'myapp',
]

REST_FRAMEWORK = {
    'DEFAULT_AUTHENTICATION_CLASSES': [
        'rest_framework_simplejwt.authentication.JWTAuthentication',
    ],
    'DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES': [
        'rest_framework.permissions.IsAuthenticated',
    ],
}

from datetime import timedelta
SIMPLE_JWT = {
    'ACCESS_TOKEN_LIFETIME': timedelta(minutes=60),
    'REFRESH_TOKEN_LIFETIME': timedelta(days=7),
    'ROTATE_REFRESH_TOKENS': True,   # new refresh token on each refresh
    'BLACKLIST_AFTER_ROTATION': True, # invalidate old refresh tokens
}

# urls.py
from rest_framework_simplejwt.views import TokenObtainPairView, TokenRefreshView

urlpatterns = [
    path('api/token/', TokenObtainPairView.as_view()),    # POST: get tokens
    path('api/token/refresh/', TokenRefreshView.as_view()),  # POST: refresh
]

# Protected view — request.user is set by JWTAuthentication
from rest_framework.views import APIView
from rest_framework.response import Response
from rest_framework.permissions import IsAuthenticated

class ProfileView(APIView):
    permission_classes = [IsAuthenticated]

    def get(self, request):
        return Response({
            'username': request.user.username,
            'email': request.user.email,
        })

# Custom user model — do this BEFORE first migration
from django.contrib.auth.models import AbstractUser

class User(AbstractUser):
    phone = models.CharField(max_length=20, blank=True)
    profile_image = models.ImageField(upload_to='profiles/', null=True, blank=True)

# settings.py
AUTH_USER_MODEL = 'myapp.User'

sections.title: Auth rules
items: Session auth: stateful, database lookup per request, great for Django views
JWT: stateless, no DB lookup to validate, standard for APIs
Access tokens: short-lived (60min). Refresh tokens: long-lived (7 days)
ROTATE_REFRESH_TOKENS: issue new refresh on each use to detect theft
Custom user model: define AUTH_USER_MODEL before first migration — can't change after

seo.metaTitle: Django JWT Authentication with simplejwt — Setup and Best Practices
seo.metaDescription: Implement Django JWT authentication: djangorestframework-simplejwt setup, access and refresh tokens, token rotation, and custom user model best practices.

speakable_v2.hook: Session auth is great for Django views, but APIs need stateless JWT — and simplejwt makes the setup straightforward.

beats.content: Session auth stores state in the database and uses a cookie. JWT is stateless — the token contains the user identity, signed by the server. Any server that knows the signing key can validate it without a database call.

Simplejwt: add JWTAuthentication to DEFAULT_AUTHENTICATION_CLASSES. POST credentials to /api/token/, get access and refresh tokens. Client includes the access token as Authorization: Bearer. When it expires, use the refresh token to get a new one.
Always create a custom User model before your first migration, even if you don't need extra fields yet. AUTH_USER_MODEL = 'myapp.User'. Changing the auth model after migrations is very painful.

speakable_v2.cap: ROTATE_REFRESH_TOKENS: True is the security setting you want — it issues a new refresh token on every use, so a stolen token can only be used once before it's detected.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Follow up with custom JWT claims for adding user roles to the token payload, or Django's permission system beyond authentication.
